cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: URL is substituted into browser command template via path.replace("%u", href) and executed via shell, potentially allowing argument delimiter injection if URL contains spaces, quotes, or shell metacharacters

connection.evidence: User-controlled URL flows directly from _goto parameter through _fork to shell execution: url -> _fork -> path.replace("%u", href) -> encoder(path) -> os.execv("/bin/sh", ["/bin/sh", "-c", path])

diff_causality.evidence: This line initiates the command execution chain by calling _fork with user URL. Reverting would prevent URL from reaching shell execution.

security_control.evidence: URL substitution into command template lacks argument delimiter neutralization
security_control.required_control: Proper argument delimitation and shell escaping for user input in command execution
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-88 requires proper delimitation when user input affects command arguments to prevent injection
existing_controls_checked: encoder() function applied to final command string
no URL-specific validation or escaping observed
security_control.deficiency_evidence: URL is directly substituted into command template without escaping shell metacharacters or argument delimiters; encoder() may not handle argument injection scenarios

concrete_impact.evidence: Potential argument injection could modify browser command behavior, but specific impact depends on browser command template and system configuration

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the URL would not be passed to _fork, preventing any potential argument injection through the browser command execution path.
supporting_evidence: URL parameter flows directly to shell execution via _fork function
Command template uses %u substitution pattern without argument delimiter escaping
Execution uses os.execv with /bin/sh -c which interprets shell metacharacters
contradicting_evidence: encoder() function is applied to the final command string, though its effectiveness against argument injection is unclear
unresolved_facts: Exact implementation and security properties of encoder() function
Default browser command template format and argument structure
Whether browser configuration is user-modifiable or trusted source only
review_comment: User-provided URLs are substituted into browser command templates and executed via shell without proper argument delimiter neutralization. The %u substitution pattern allows URL content to affect command arguments if it contains spaces, quotes, or shell metacharacters. Use shell escaping or parameterized execution to separate URL from command arguments, such as passing URL as a separate argument rather than string interpolation.
